options: Declares a new variable with a default value
Builds a new list or map by looping over an existing one
Deletes a resource after a set number of runs
Converts a string into a number
questions.explain: A for expression loops over an existing list or map and collects the results into a new list or map, such as generating instance names from a count.
range(3) produces the number sequence [0, 1, 2] — a zero-indexed list of three values, commonly looped over with a for expression.

questions.q: How is a conditional expression written in HCL?
options: when condition then true_value otherwise false_value
questions.explain: HCL's conditional expression follows the pattern condition ? true_value : false_value, evaluating to one or the other based on whether the condition is true.

questions.q: What advantage does lookup(map, key, default) have over directly indexing map[key]?
options: It falls back to a default value instead of erroring if the key is missing
It only works with lists, not maps
It automatically creates the key if missing
questions.explain: lookup() accepts a default value to return if the key isn't present, avoiding the error that direct map indexing would throw on a missing key.

questions.q: What does the templatefile() function do?
options: Deletes a template file from disk
Reads a file from disk and substitutes variables into its contents
Converts a .tf file into a .tfvars file
Creates a new Terraform module from scratch
questions.explain: templatefile() reads a file's contents and substitutes the supplied variables into it, commonly used to render a startup script per environment.
